chunks: From him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman who is incapacitated and lost her mind: Is her sale and her giving in charity permissible? He said, 'No.' And regarding the divorce of the drunkard and his freeing of slaves, he said, 'It is not permissible.'

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةِ الْمَعْتُوهَةِ: The incapacitated woman (one with mental deficiency)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal status of a drunkard's divorce and a mentally incapacitated woman's property transactions in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of *al-ma'tuwhah* (a woman with diminished but not absent intellect), ruling that her property transactions and charity are invalid due to lack of full legal capacity. It further extends this principle of invalidity to the divorce and manumission of slaves by a drunkard, emphasizing that intoxication negates the requisite mental clarity for binding legal acts in Shia fiqh. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *'aql* (intellect/reason) as a prerequisite for valid *fi'l shar'i* (legal action).
